overview: White throws the g-pawn forward at once, hoping to hit Black's knight and open the g-file. After 2...Nxg4 Black is a pawn up and White needs quick development and e4 to justify it. Few strong players choose it, and Black can simply decline with 2...d5.

white_ideas.idea: Open the g-file for the rook and bishop on g2
Develop fast with e4 and Bc4 while Black grabs material

black_ideas.idea: Take 2...Nxg4 and return the pawn at the right moment

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after e4 with Black a pawn up
Black king keeps the extra pawn, White pawns split on the kingside

character.notes: Wild, forcing, with a wing pawn thrown forward on move two; Black has to find precise defence.

gambit.notes: 2.g4 Nxg4 leaves Black a clean pawn up and White must prove compensation with development.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; Black simply takes the pawn or plays ...d5 and White has loosened the kingside.

structure.notes: After e4 and ...d5 the centre is tense and undecided.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever play 2.g4 against 1...Nf6; it is a surprise weapon.

level.notes: Not a good repertoire choice since it loses a pawn for little; no one learns it as a first line.

sublines_that_differ.name: 2...d5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black declines, 3.g5 Ne4 and White is already a tempo down with a loosened kingside.

character.reason: An early g4 pawn sacrifice makes the game concrete and double-edged.

gambit.reason: White offers the g-pawn on move two and Black can keep it with 2...Nxg4.

soundness.reason: Strong players regard 2.g4 as a loosening pawn sacrifice that scores through surprise.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and mostly depends on whether e4 and ...d5 arrive.

approach.reason: Strong players seldom choose 2.g4 at all.

level.reason: A dubious line is never Beginner and the plans are not hard enough for Advanced.

plans.reason: White offers a pawn for development and pushes wing pawns.
